accepted.s: Janani Suraksha Yojana, launched in 2005, primarily provides which of the following support?
o: Cash assistance to pregnant women for institutional delivery
Free antenatal care on the ninth day of every month
Weekly iron and folic acid supplementation to adolescents
Digital vaccination records for children aged 0–16 years
accepted.x: Janani Suraksha Yojana was launched in 2005 to provide cash assistance for institutional deliveries, with particular focus on BPL, SC and ST women.
accepted.tq: Match the programme with its distinctive benefit rather than its launch year alone.
accepted.sec: Health programmes → launch year and target group  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA), consider the following statements:
1. It was launched in 2016.
2. It focuses on pregnant women in the second and third trimesters.
3. Free antenatal care is provided on the ninth day of every month.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: PMSMA was launched in 2016 for pregnant women in the second and third trimesters and provides free antenatal care on the ninth day of every month.
accepted.tq: Check the programme’s launch year, beneficiary group and fixed service day together.
accepted.sec: Health programmes → launch year and target group  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which one of the following is correctly matched?

Programme — Primary focus

1. PMSMA — Free antenatal care on the ninth day of every month
2. Janani Suraksha Yojana — Cash support for institutional delivery
3. U-WIN — Digital vaccination registry
4. RKSK — Adolescent health services

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four pairings are correct: PMSMA concerns antenatal care, JSY institutional delivery assistance, U-WIN vaccination records, and RKSK adolescent health.

accepted.sec: Health programmes → launch year and target group  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The U-WIN platform is primarily intended to maintain a digital vaccination registry for which group?
o: Children up to 6 years and elderly persons
All adults receiving health insurance benefits
Pregnant women and children from birth to 16 years
accepted.x: U-WIN, launched in 2024, is a digital vaccination registry for pregnant women and children in the 0–16 age group.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between a vaccination registry and programmes dealing with adolescent or maternal care.
accepted.sec: Health programmes → launch year and target group  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?

1. AB School Health and Wellness Programme — Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and Ministry of Education
2. MAA — Breastfeeding promotion
3. CLMC/LMU — Donor human milk
4. U-WIN — Weekly iron and folic acid supplementation for adolescents
accepted.x: U-WIN is a digital vaccination registry for pregnant women and children aged 0–16 years. Weekly iron and folic acid supplementation is associated with adolescent health interventions under RKSK.
accepted.tq: Find the programme whose target service is swapped with that of a nearby programme.
accepted.sec: Health programmes → launch year and target group  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the National Rural Health Mission is correct?

1. Its rural health delivery system has ASHA and ANM personnel as an important backbone.
2. Along with the National Urban Health Mission, it forms the National Health Mission.
3. It is concerned exclusively with urban health services.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: NRHM serves the rural population and relies on ASHA and ANM personnel. Together with NUHM, it forms the National Health Mission; it is not an urban-only programme.
accepted.tq: Reject the statement containing an exclusive and reversed target group.
accepted.sec: Health programmes → launch year and target group  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between NRHM, NUHM and NHM?
o: NRHM is a component of the urban-only NHM
NHM and NRHM together constitute NUHM
NRHM and NUHM together constitute NHM
NUHM is the rural component of NRHM
accepted.x: The National Rural Health Mission and National Urban Health Mission together form the National Health Mission.
accepted.tq: Separate the rural, urban and umbrella components of a health mission.
accepted.sec: Health programmes → launch year and target group  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Family Physician concept in Andhra Pradesh, primary healthcare is extended to villages through:
o: Mobile vaccination teams operating only during epidemics
Specialist doctors visiting only district headquarters
Telemedicine consultations conducted exclusively from private hospitals
PHC doctors visiting villages on fixed days through 104 mobile units
accepted.x: Under the Family Physician concept, PHC doctors visit villages on fixed days through 104 mobile units. Village health clinics function at the village secretariat level.
accepted.tq: Apply the institutional arrangement to identify who visits villages and through which platform.
accepted.sec: AP healthcare - Aarogyasri / NTR Vaidya Seva, Family Physician, telemedicine, village clinics  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Village health clinics under the Andhra Pradesh healthcare model are established at which level?
accepted.x: The village health clinics are located at the village secretariat level, complementing the Family Physician system.
accepted.tq: Use the location clue to distinguish grassroots health facilities from higher administrative institutions.
accepted.sec: AP healthcare - Aarogyasri / NTR Vaidya Seva, Family Physician, telemedicine, village clinics  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Human capital is best understood as the:
o: Annual income generated by the working population
Total physical capital owned by households and firms
Number of persons employed in the manufacturing sector
Stock of skills, knowledge and health embodied in people
accepted.x: Human capital refers to the stock of skills, knowledge and health possessed by people.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a stock of human attributes from income, employment and physical assets.
accepted.sec: Human capital formation - concept, drivers  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following are recognised means of human capital formation?

1. Investment in education
2. Investment in health
3. On-the-job training
4. Migration and information

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Human capital is formed through investment in education, health, on-the-job training, migration and information.
accepted.tq: Treat the less obvious drivers, such as migration and information, as part of the complete list.
accepted.sec: Human capital formation - concept, drivers  [other exams]

accepted.s: Why is human capital formation considered central to inclusive growth?
o: It replaces all physical capital with public expenditure
It confines investment to already productive urban workers
It expands capabilities through education, health and skills across sections of society
It measures only the size of the labour force
accepted.x: Human capital formation supports inclusive growth by improving education, health and skills, thereby expanding capabilities across society.
accepted.tq: Select the option expressing the broad developmental effect rather than a narrow resource measure.
accepted.sec: Human capital formation - concept, drivers  [other exams]

accepted.s: The focus described in Economic Survey 2025–26 on education and health indicates a shift:
o: From public health to physical infrastructure exclusively
From access to quality and learning outcomes, along with preventive care
From quality to enrolment alone, without concern for outcomes
From preventive care to curative care alone
accepted.x: The stated policy shift is from access towards quality and learning outcomes, together with preventive care. Obesity and digital addiction are also emerging concerns.
accepted.tq: Identify the direction of the policy shift and reject its reversed formulation.
accepted.sec: Human capital formation - concept, drivers  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly expresses the concern about the ‘missing middle’ in India’s health-financing system?
o: About 40 crore people remain inadequately covered between public support and formal insurance arrangements
About 40 lakh people are excluded from all school-meal programmes
About 40 crore adolescents are covered only by RKSK
About 40 per cent of villages lack a village secretariat
accepted.x: The term ‘missing middle’ refers to approximately 40 crore people who remain inadequately covered by existing health-financing arrangements.
accepted.tq: Apply the policy term to the population-coverage problem rather than to education or administration.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
